investmentThesis:
This is Bugatti's first residential tower in the United States. Dubai is the marque's inaugural residential project, under another developer. Prosper Group and Belgium's Versluys Group closed the site for $50 million in August 2026, a $650 million stated development, on a parcel carved from the adjacent One Brickell Riverfront holding rather than found on the open market.

Versluys Group, founded in 1908 and led by CEO Bart Versluys with COO Peter De Decker, has spent more than a century on high-end coastal work in Belgium and the Netherlands, including the renovation of La Réserve in Knokke-Heist. This is the firm's U.S. entry, paired with Prosper under CEO Jay Roberts.

Sales are expected in the first half of 2027, with no price schedule published. Registering now is the way to hold a position before public launch.

name: Bugatti Residences Miami
residenceContent:
Bugatti Residences Miami rises 60 stories on a roughly one-acre Miami River assemblage at 75 SW Miami Avenue Road, with more than 300 feet of river frontage that opens east toward Biscayne Bay and the Downtown skyline. The site sits in Brickell's urban core, near Brickell City Centre, Interstate 95, Brightline, and Miami International.

Brandon Haw Architecture leads the design, drawing on Bugatti's C-line for the tower form. Interiors are by George Yabu and Glenn Pushelberg. Floor plans, finishes, and the full amenity program have not been released.

Bugatti named Rhodium as exclusive global residential operating partner, with a program defined by white-glove butler service.
